proposals.title: Yannai A. Gonczarowski, Ori Heffetz and Clayton Thomas — Strategyproofness-Exposing Descriptions of Matching Mechanisms
proposals.date_scope: Author preprint, arXiv 2209.13148v4, September 9, 2026. Cover and versioned primary URL inspected; exact-version PDF equals the retrieved unversioned body byte for byte. No claim of journal publication.
proposals.use: Noncircular fixed-menu route to individual proposer strategy-proofness. Chapter supplies the finite unmatched-set lemma, schedule coupling and truncation-prefix details rather than invoking them without proof.

inspection.body_scope: Physical 1; 7–14 (printed 6–13: strict reports, partial lists/outside in footnote 7, DA, menu definitions, opposite-side Description 1 and main proof); Appendix B physical 36 bottom through 38 opening (printed A.4–A.6). Many-to-one remarks on A.6 read only to delimit scope.

image_scope.checked: Authors, title, September 9, 2026 and arXiv v4.
Strict one-to-one domain and partial-list/outside convention.
Description 1 uses institution-proposing DA without the applicant, not applicant-proposing DA.
Singleton and strictly-above truncation arguments in the noncircular Appendix B proof.

proposals.limits: The main-text proof on printed 13 assumes strategy-proofness and cannot establish it. Appendix B invokes unmatched-set invariance and abbreviates the truncation reasoning; both are proved. No group, capacity, substitutes-with-contracts, tie, TTC, communication-complexity or experimental theorem is claimed.

proposals.title: Rafael Pass — A Course in Networks and Markets, Chapter 8: Matching Markets
proposals.date_scope: Author-hosted HTML. Title page names Rafael Pass alone. Copyright page says ©2018 and catalogues MIT Press [2019]; preserve that distinction rather than inventing an edition date.
proposals.use: Assignment utility and ownership accounting; our direct nonnegative price/utility upper bound gives a complete certificate for all feasible partial assignments, including a forbidden edge.

inspection.body_scope: Sections 8.1–8.3: unit-demand valuation-minus-price model; outside allocation; preferred-choice graph/market clearing; cancellation of payments and proof of welfare optimality. Title and copyright pages read separately.

proposals.limits: No reliance on the general price-existence algorithm of section 8.4, Hall theorem, general LP integrality, budgets-as-quasilinear equivalence, or source examples. Cornell Chapter 14 was discovery reading only; its abbreviated complete-market incentive proof is not a relied source.

proposals.title: Yann Bramoullé, Rachel Kranton and Martin D’Amours — Strategic Interaction and Networks
proposals.date_scope: Final published article, American Economic Review 104(3), 898–930, March 2014; author publication page labels it final. The upload path contains 2016/09 and is not the article date.
proposals.use: Economic interpretation of complements/substitutes and boundary active-set logic. Our finite path/two-agent solutions, contraction proof, planner square completion and funding incidence are derived independently.

inspection.body_scope: I.A–C, printed 901–904 / physical 4–7: game, quadratic payoff, nonnegative best replies and active sets. V.C printed 918–919 / physical 21–22: endogenous peer outcomes, constraints and selection cautions. VI.A printed 919–920 / physical 22–23: complements, nonexistence and caps. Appendix printed 921–922 / physical 24–25: active-set proof and quadratic potential conditions.

image_scope.checked: Negative cross term, max(0,·) best reply and stated base parameter domain.
Complementarity amplification/nonexistence, capped best reply, and scope of sufficient curvature conditions.

proposals.limits: Do not conflate the potential with aggregate welfare, own-action concavity with uniqueness, or an inverse matrix with a feasible equilibrium. No general spectral characterization, asymptotic stability, directed-network or empirical-identification result is asserted without its own proof. The gamma=2 two-agent case is independently proved outside the paper’s base delta∈[0,1].

proposals.title: Matthew O. Jackson — A Survey of Models of Network Formation: Stability and Efficiency
proposals.date_scope: Author-hosted body: January 2003; revision November 29, 2003. Cover footnote says the book chapter appears in 2005, while current author listing says 2004. Cite the inspected revised manuscript, not an inferred publication year.
proposals.use: Primary exposition by a co-originator of the connections model, attributed there to Jackson–Wolinsky (1996). Our three-node all-graph classification, equality boundaries and contract-conditioned transfers are proved directly.

inspection.body_scope: Cover; printed/physical 12, Example 1 connections model; 21–22, pairwise stability and its single-link/coalition limits; 32–34, efficiency definitions and connections-model comparison.

image_scope.checked: Distance-discounted benefit, per-endpoint costs and three-node path payoff form.
Unilateral deletion and absent-edge weak/strict consent convention.

proposals.limits: This is an actually inspected author survey, not a claim that the original 1996 article was read. No general-n classification, convergence-to-efficiency, coalition stability or empirical causal-network conclusion is imported.

originality: Preference and priority profiles, valuation matrices, funding rules, numeric interventions, problems and prose are original. The five sources support methods at the stated scopes; no copied source problems or whole-document verification claim.

Its source record was read by the coordinator; the coordinator additionally inspected the menu-proof Appendix B and one page image. Actual specialist inspection is stated separately above.
